candidate.answerReason: The relative speed is 120 mph, so the driver encounters a 10-mile stretch of westbound traffic in five minutes. The resulting estimate is 200 vehicles per 100 miles, and endpoint uncertainty cannot change the closest choice.

methods.label: Use relative speed to estimate the spacing
methods.explanation:
Because the vehicles approach one another, their speeds add. The westbound traffic moves past the driver at \(60+60=120\) miles per hour. Five minutes is \(1/12\) hour, so the driver encounters a stretch of westbound traffic of length
\[
120\cdot\frac1{12}=10\text{ miles}.
\]
Twenty vehicles in about \(10\) miles suggests \(2\) vehicles per mile, or about \(200\) in \(100\) miles.

The interval endpoints do not make this estimate exact, but we can check that they cannot change the choice. Let \(s>0\) be the spacing in miles. The \(20\) encountered vehicles span \(19\) complete gaps. The observation interval extends at most one spacing before the first vehicle and after the last, so
\[
19s\le10\le21s.
\]
Consequently \(190\le100/s\le210\). If \(N\) vehicles occupy a \(100\)-mile section, the same gap reasoning gives
\[
(N-1)s\le100\le(N+1)s,
\]
so \(189\le N\le211\). Every count in this range is closest to \(\boxed{200}\) among the offered values. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses elementary relative motion, time conversion, proportional scaling, and the relationship between equally spaced points and gaps.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is translating opposite-direction motion into the distance of traffic encountered. Direct proportion converts that distance into a vehicle-count estimate. The written endpoint check also uses the point-and-gap relationship. Time conversion, distance equals speed times time, and ratio meaning support the route.
limitations: The positions of the observation and highway-section endpoints do not determine an exact vehicle count, but the closest offered value is uniquely determined.

review.mathematicalCheck: Relative motion covers 120·(5/60)=10 miles. The justified endpoint bounds give 190≤100/s≤210 and consequently 189≤N≤211. Every count in this conservative range is closest to 200.
